clue.text: Models deem breaks intrusive

indicators.note: breaks tells us the words models deem are smashed up and their letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Fashion models who barge in where they are not wanted are being pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges MODELSDEEM; 'deem breaks' reads as a verb phrase but 'breaks' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who interferes in others' affairs is being nosy and pushy.

clue.text: Debunk the synthetic

explanation.surface: Exposing the falsity of something artificial.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule or deflate something is one sense; an imitation or fake product, as in mock leather, is the other.

clue.text: Cheat lots of people out of gifts

parts.note: to do someone is slang for swindling them
nations are whole peoples, lots of people at once

explanation.surface: Swindling a crowd out of their presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is a link meaning the answer is made from these pieces, not a removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents given to charity or a cause are contributions, a synonym.

clue.text: Making money in Britain, owns a place abroad

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, British money
to own something is to have it, so owns gives has

explanation.surface: Someone earning British money and buying a property overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the Latin libra, used in the pound sign; 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan capital is a city far from Britain, so a foreign location.

clue.text: Keeping the Latin Quarter in view is an artful trick

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a view is a sight
the Latin Quarter is in Paris, so the word the is given in French

explanation.surface: Watching over the Parisian district is a cunning ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin Quarter is a district of Paris, so 'the' is wanted in French; 'Keeping ... in view' reads as watching, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is deft trickery, a cunning manoeuvre.

clue.text: Grew older, dull, and awfully rude

parts.note: matt or mat describes a dull, unglossy finish

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word rude is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone aged and became boring and very impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull' reads as boring but means a flat, unglossy finish; 'awfully' is the anagram signal, not an intensifier for rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripened or aged, as wine or cheese does over time.

clue.text: Car hired for a team of irregulars?

explanation.surface: Hiring a cab to carry a band of irregular soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football a taxi squad is the group of reserve players kept off the regular roster.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for paid rides is one sense; the reserve squad in American football, outside the regular roster, is the other.

clue.text: Likely holding of Parisian expert

indicators.note: holding means one word clasps another inside it

parts.note: apt means likely or inclined to
a Parisian says de for of

explanation.surface: A probable possession of a skilled man from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' asks for the French word for 'of'; 'holding' is the container signal, and 'Likely' is a synonym, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled person, a master of a craft.

clue.text: Form relatively close personal ties

parts.note: relatively plays on relatives: the ties are weddings between people of the same family or between different groups

explanation.surface: Forming fairly close friendships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean fairly, but it points to relations becoming linked by wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed within a group or between groups, binding families together.

clue.text: Pass a portion that's really liberal

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
some means a portion of something

explanation.surface: Giving a share that is truly generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or sum is a generous, sizeable one.

clue.text: Scots can not get this tropical plant

explanation.surface: Scottish people cannot obtain an exotic bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish dialect for cannot is one sense; a tropical flowering plant with broad leaves is the other.

clue.text: Very green gregarious type

parts.note: extra means very, as in extra large
vert is green in heraldry and in French

explanation.surface: An extremely inexperienced person who loves company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' seems to mean naive, but it is the heraldic colour VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person, the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Street guide for the foreigner

parts.note: a Ranger is a senior member of the Girl Guides, and also a park guide

explanation.surface: A local guide shows an outsider around the street.
explanation.walkthrough: In British Guiding, Rangers are the oldest section of the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider or alien, someone unknown to a place.

clue.text: Put off some women with crude terminology

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken, giving letters lurking within them

explanation.surface: Coarse language from certain women discourages people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to letters inside 'crude terminology'; 'women with' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage or dissuade someone from acting.

clue.text: Went down and gave a very generous gratuity

explanation.surface: Someone fell over and left a lavish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppled or capsized is one sense; rewarded a waiter too lavishly is the other.

clue.text: Wild flower to be seen round the North

indicators.note: round means the flower word encircles the other letter

parts.note: a violet is a flower
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An untamed bloom growing in the northern part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a bloom here, not a river; VIOLET goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild in the sense of fierce, raging or uncontrolled.

clue.text: Support demonstration

parts.note: a public vote is a show of backing, so the phrase describes a ballot

explanation.surface: A rally held in support of a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a protest march; the demonstration is instead people showing their backing at the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll in which voters choose candidates shows how much backing each has.

clue.text: Scene calling for ten in stage presentation

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a drama is a play put on stage
ten written as figures looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A setting that needs ten actors in a theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' gives IO, the figures 1 and 0 read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A model three-dimensional tableau representing a view or landscape.

clue.text: Confidence man's profession?

explanation.surface: The trade of a confidence trickster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidence man' looks like one unit, a con man, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-confidence or certainty is one sense; the life-cover business, the trade of an insurance man, is the other.

clue.text: Characteristic consideration

explanation.surface: A distinctive trait of thoughtfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular aspect or detail, as in in this regard, is one sense; regard and esteem for others is the other.

clue.text: Nothing but one river in another river makes a rushing stream

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed within the other river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
O looks like zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Watercourses merging to create a fast-flowing flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a long river in the English Midlands; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, fast-flowing body of water.

clue.text: He'll put a good finish on wooden furniture

definitions.text: He'll put a good finish on

explanation.surface: A craftsman who polishes timber furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: One who prepares or finishes surfaces such as stone or leather is one sense; a kitchen sideboard with shelves is the other.

clue.text: Far from cool

explanation.surface: Remote and chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote in space is one sense; aloof or unfriendly in manner is the other.

clue.text: Popular place to feed in

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A trendy spot for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun, a venue, but it is the verb put.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data into a computer is to supply or load it.

clue.text: Groom about to be committed to prison

indicators.note: committed to suggests being locked inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: pen is slang for a penitentiary, a prison
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bridegroom facing a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the man at a wedding but is the verb, to tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy one's appearance or plumage, as birds do.

clue.text: Herb's got two girls

definitions.note: read as herb has, with the herb as subject

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
Mary is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A man called Herb is dating two women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name, but it is a plant; the 's means has.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic shrub used in cooking, a kitchen plant.

clue.text: Among mixed fruit

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the word among are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something tossed in among the fruit salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Not all little troubles seem minor

indicators.note: not all means just part of the words that follow is used, a run hiding inside them

explanation.surface: Small worries are not entirely trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' points to a run inside 'troubles seem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser or smaller in importance, as in of less account.

clue.text: Men hope an error can be found, but they're exceptional

indicators.note: an error means the words men hope an are written down wrongly, scrambled

explanation.surface: Men hoping for a mistake, though they are remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges MENHOPEAN; 'can be found, but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable people or marvels are prodigies, outstanding things.

clue.text: Nobody has caught cold-for the present

indicators.note: has caught means the first word traps the second inside it

parts.note: none means nobody
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: No one has picked up a chill at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught cold' reads as falling ill, but C is held inside NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic for the present occasion, kept in the phrase for the time being.

clue.text: Figure one's accomplished

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a figure
the word one, with the possessive giving no letters

explanation.surface: A number that has been achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' gives D, the Roman numeral 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Completed or finished, a task achieved.

clue.text: Such dealers get no rest. It's a mistake

indicators.note: mistake means the letters of no rest and it's a are muddled up

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers who never get a break call it an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' rearranges NORESTITSA; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers selling paper, pens and office supplies are traders of this kind.
